messages.author: 122cdbf8c559091c
messages.subject: SEM: highly correlated variables
parts:
Hi,

I started using lavaan for SEM (love it much more than SPSS/AMOS, what an eye-opener!).
My question is probably more theoretical...

I have a model with various biological measurements (cross-sectional): brain volume, amyloid accumulation and tau pathology in the brain.
However, for tau pathology I included two different regions, with the idea that region A accumulates pathology before region B.
Region A would lead to brain volume loss and this would lead to tau in region B.

Thus:
Tau region A -> volume loss -> tau region B

The problem is that tau in region A and region B are highly correlated (r = 0.7) and when making the SEM model, the model indices are not good.
The model becomes only acceptable when I create a path from region A to region B (making the path volume loss -> region B insignificant).

Is there a way to solve this? Or are these the limitations of the data I have to accept?

Many thanks!
Best
H

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: SEM: highly correlated variables
parts: Is there a way to solve this? Or are these the limitations of the data I have to accept?

You can post non-lavaan questions to the general forum SEMNET:

http://www2.gsu.edu/~mkteer/semnet.html

Sounds like you "solved" it by adding the direct path between Tau in the 2 regions.  That model fits better than the model that proposed 100% of the relationship is mediated via volume loss, so your data is telling you the worse fitting model is not as good of a representation of the data.

But your data might not even be able to answer your research question.  Were they all measured at the same time?  A causal process takes time to unfold, so how long does Tau take to decrease volume, and how much time before that decrease in volume affects Tau in the other region?  Those times would need to be built into your research design.  You might find it helpful to read about longitudinal mediation models:

http://dx.doi.org/10.1037/0021-843X.112.4.558

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
UvA web page: http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

Unfortunately, we do not yet have enough longitudinal data to model that... so, yes right now everything is measured at time point 1 and that might indeed be the limitation ( I thought that this might somehow be modeled into the model (not sure how), but that is probably too farfetched).
Thank you!
